Meristem Type/Component: Shoot Apical Meristem (SAM) - Histological Zones (CZ, PZ, RM/RZ)
Key Signaling Pathways: WUS-CLV Signaling Loop (WUS, CLV1, CLV2, CLV3, BAM1)
Establishing Findings: The SAM consists of the Central Zone (CZ) harboring stem cells, the Peripheral Zone (PZ) for lateral organ primordia, and the Rib Meristem (RM/RZ) for stem development. The WUS-CLV axis acts as a self-correcting rheostat: WUS in the Organizing Center (OC) maintains CZ stem cells, while CLV3 peptide from the CZ signals through receptors (CLV1, BAM1, CLV2) to repress WUS.
Hormonal and Environmental Regulators: Cytokinin (CK) induces WUS via AHK2/AHK4 receptors to maintain stemness; Auxin promotes differentiation and organogenesis at the PZ. Low night temperatures ( $6-12 \text{°C}$ ) or high light disrupt this network, often increasing locule number. Salt stress reduces cell division via GA/DELLA pathways.
Crop-Specific Findings: In Tomato, mutations in  lc  (near  WUS ) and  fas  ( CLV3  promoter) increase locule counts (2-15+). In Maize,  CT2  (G $\alpha$ ) binds  FEA2  (CLV2 ortholog) to limit SAM size. Rice  LOG  mutants show reduced meristem size.
Unresolved Questions (Inferred): How specific epigenetic marks established during temperature stress persist through developmental transitions; the precise mechanism of non-transcriptional WUS protein movement via plasmodesmata.
Research Gaps (Inferred): Detailed epigenetic mapping of  WUS  loci (e.g., H3K27me3) and CRISPR-based verification of non-coding regulatory elements in non-model crops to map CLV-independent pathways.

Key Signaling Pathways: AG-WUS Loop (AG, KNU, MIF2, CRC, TFL2/LHP1)
Establishing Findings: Unlike the SAM, the FM must terminate. AG terminates the FM by repressing WUS through Polycomb recruitment (early stage) and activating KNU (stage 6). KNU displaces the chromatin remodeler SYD and recruits HDA19/TPL complexes to silence WUS. Mutations in CLV or CK treatment synergistically increase carpel/locule number.
Hormonal and Environmental Regulators: High temperature inhibits Brassinosteroid (BR) biosynthesis and  SlCRCa  expression, preventing timely WUS termination and causing malformed fruit. Cytokinin positively regulates locule formation via  CYP735A1 . Auxin maximum during carpel initiation reduces FM activity.
Crop-Specific Findings: In Tomato,  SlKNU  mutants show 30–50% increases in locule number;  SlCLE9  provides genetic redundancy when  SlCLV3  is lost. In Arabidopsis,  clv1  and  clv3  mutants show increased organ numbers.
Unresolved Questions (Inferred): The threshold of cytokinin or heat stress required to irreversibly disrupt the CLV3-WUS balance or bypass the termination signal; how GA crosstalk alters locule-specific loops.
Research Gaps (Inferred): Lack of definitive studies on how epigenetic 'memory' of heat stress influences FM determinacy; use of CRISPR to target specific ARR response elements to decouple growth from termination.

Establishing Findings: Meristems harbor intrinsic hypoxic niches and core developmental priming genes (STM, ATHB13, WRKY6) for stress plasticity. G-proteins regulate pedicel formation and flowering time. Stem cell homeostasis relies on the antagonism between proliferation (WUS) and differentiation (CLV).
Hormonal and Environmental Regulators: Salt Stress (NaCl):  clv3-2  and  clv1 bam1  mutants show enhanced tolerance. ABA signaling (ATHB33), Brassinosteroids, and hypoxia set the pace of meristem activity. Photoperiod and GA (via RGG2) influence G-protein regulated growth.
Crop-Specific Findings: In Tomato,  $G\beta$  ( SlGB1 ) mutation leads to SAM lethality via phenolic amide accumulation. Maize  ct2  mutants show robust inflorescence branching due to enlarged meristems.
Unresolved Questions (Inferred): Interaction between hypoxia-inducible factors and G-protein signaling under osmotic stress; how G-protein modulators alter the termination signal during indeterminate growth.
Research Gaps (Inferred): Higher-resolution spatiotemporal mapping of G-protein signaling within the CZ vs PZ; CRISPR-based investigation of tissue-specific compensation by CLE-paralogs under field stress.

Establishing Findings: RAM maintenance is modulated by peptide-receptor modules. CLE14 triggers differentiation and exhaustion under phosphate deficiency by suppressing SHR-SCR and PIN-auxin pathways. IDA controls cell separation during lateral root emergence.
Hormonal and Environmental Regulators: Phosphate (Pi) deficiency, Nitrogen (N) deficiency, and salinity/alkali stress. Auxin transport (PIN2) and glucose-sugar metabolism regulate gravitropism and initiation.
Crop-Specific Findings: In Cucumber,  GPA1  positively regulates root growth; in Sorghum and Maize, the  $G\gamma$  subunit  AT1  regulates  $H_{2}O_{2}$  distribution for alkali tolerance.
Unresolved Questions (Inferred): Whether standard RGF developmental pathways are identical to nutrient-stress triggered pathways; the precise downstream effectors of G-protein-mediated  $Ca^{2+}$  signaling.
Research Gaps (Inferred): Molecular mechanisms of peptide transport from roots to shoots during systemic stress; CRISPR-mediated editing to separate root nutrient foraging from shoot pleiotropy.

Establishing Findings: TPX2 activates Aurora A kinase; CDC20.1 regulates meiotic chromosome segregation. The CLE45–SKM1/2 module sustains pollen tube growth to ensure seed production during high-temperature stress.
Hormonal and Environmental Regulators: Salt stress triggers microtubule breakdown; GA biosynthetic mutants show enhanced survival under salt stress. Heat stress (30  $\text{°C}$ ) activates the CLE45-SKM1 interaction.
Crop-Specific Findings: Arabidopsis  Ler  is more sensitive to salt than  Col-0 . Tomato shows drought-induced flower drop regulated by  SlPhyt2  and PSK signaling.
Unresolved Questions (Inferred): Whether chromosome segregation genes directly mediate salt tolerance or post-stress recovery; the mechanism by which SKM1/2 prevents premature pollen tube termination.
Research Gaps (Inferred): Efficacy of CRISPR-Cas9 in targeting SAC components to modify locule number under thermal stress; manipulation of subtilases like  SlPhyt2  to prevent flower abortion.
